subject: Performance SLO & load test coordination — FinWise
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@finwise.com>, Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & load test coordination — FinWise

Tom / Sally — thanks again for today’s call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Summary of targets you shared:
- P95 latency: <= 200ms for synchronous text generation (single-turn requests)
- Streaming/long-running flows: initial token latency <= 120ms, sustained stream throughput to support 20 concurrent streams
- Expected sustained throughput: ~350 requests/sec during peak window; burst to 800rps for 2–3 minutes
- Concurrency target: 150 concurrent model contexts

What we need from you to run a customer-led test (we can host or you can run k6/Locust against our endpoints):
1) Preferred test window (2–4 hour window, off-hours preferred) — you suggested May 4–6 range.
2) k6 or Locust script (if you have one, please share) — we can also provide a starter k6 script.
3) Test account details, or if you want Redwood to create a temp test account, we’ll send credentials.
4) IP allowlist for load generators (so we can open firewall rules).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm test window and share script (or tell us if you want the Redwood-provided script).
- We’ll provision a scoped test account and send allowlist ranges and any required headers/auth.
- Marissa will be your Redwood tech lead for the run and will monitor telemetry and SLO gates.

Attaching: starter k6 script (we’ll follow up with a slightly modified version once we review your script).

Thanks — I’ll loop Rishi and Marissa on technicals.
— Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_k6_starter.js (stub)

From: Tom Li <tom.li@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@finwise.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & load test coordination — FinWise

Thanks Logan — great summary. We’re aligned on the SLOs and the window. A few clarifications and answers: 

- Test window: May 5, 02:00–06:00 UTC (our ops prefers early-morning).
- We’ll run k6 from our infra and will share the script. We prefer k6 (already have infra); I’ll attach the current version.
- Expected traffic: we'll target 400rps sustained with 1,000rps short burst to validate autoscaling.
- Auth: we can use a test API key pair if you can create one.
- IP allowlist: we will provide the list of load generator IPs in a follow-up email.

I’ve attached our k6 script (finwise_k6_script_v1.js). It contains the scenario we plan to run (mix of streaming calls and short sync calls). We’ll also include a readme with the sequence and expected payloads.

Can Marissa or Rishi confirm any request headers and token scopes we should use? Also, do you have rate-limiting guidance for pre-test warmup?

 Tom
Tom Li
Head of Platform
FinWise

Attachment: finwise_k6_script_v1.js (stub)

Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & load test coordination — FinWise

Appreciate the quick reply, Tom. We’ve created a scoped test account and provisional API key for FinWise: 
- Test account: finwise-loadtest-2027
- API key ID: test_FinWise_2027_01 (we’ll send the secret over the secure channel)

IP allowlist ranges (please add to your outbound firewall so our ops can accept the traffic from your load generators):
- 34.201.120.0/24
- 52.10.44.0/24
- 18.205.0.0/16 (regional pool for burst)

Request/headers guidance from our side (Marissa / Rishi — please confirm):
- Use standard Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY_SECRET> header.
- For streaming tests, use the /v1/streams generate endpoint and include X-Client-Request-Id for traceability.
- Token scopes: test:inference (read-only for test account).
- Warmup recommendation: ramp to 25% of target over 10 minutes, hold 5 minutes, then ramp to 100% over 15 minutes.

We’ll run a brief smoke test 24 hours prior (May 4) to validate connectivity and routing. Marissa will monitor metrics and keep Slack channel #finwise-loadtest updated.

Attaching: redwood_test_account_instructions.pdf (network and auth details)

 Logan

Attachment: redwood_test_account_instructions.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@finwise.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sally Nguyen <sally.nguyen@finwise.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & load test coordination — FinWise

Looping in a quick tech checklist for the run and a couple notes from our infra review: 

Checklist:
- Endpoint: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate (sync) and https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams (streaming).
- Auth: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY_SECRET> (we’ll provide secret via secure vault link).
- Headers: X-Client-Request-Id, X-Test-Run: finwise-2027-05-05.
- Response size: please use the sample payloads attached in your script; larger-than-normal payloads may increase latency.
- Concurrency limit: we’ll cap active model contexts at 200 for the test; if you need more, notify Rishi.

Observability / SLO gates we’ll watch in real time:
- P50 / P95 latency for sync calls
- Initial token latency and token throughput for streams
- Error rate (5xx) and increased retry patterns
- Token billing counters (to validate cost/throughput)

Warmup note: during the warmup and ramp we’ll also enable KV cache priming for common prefixes — that should improve p50 but we’ll watch p95 closely.

I’ll join the run and will share a short post-run summary with latency histograms and any anomalies. If anything looks off we’ll trigger an automated rollback to a lower-capacity pool.

 Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Li <tom.li@finwise.com>

Thanks everyone — all set on our side. Confirming: May 5, 02:00–06:00 UTC. We’ll run the attached k6 script and will post results to the shared drive and Slack channel. We’ve uploaded our IP list to the Drive link and included a short readme.

One quick ask: after the run can Redwood share a short slide with the key SLO outcomes (P50/P95, errors, CPU/GPU utilization) and any recommended next steps for production tuning? We can present that in our ops review on May 10.

I’ll send the load generator IP list and the k6 invocation command in a separate message to ops.

 Tom
